title: SpecArch specification, meta-model 0.3
description: A SpecArch specification describes one system through its whole life cycle: the sources it rests on, the requirements (stakeholders, needs, requirements, glossary, assumptions, constraints), the design (enums, entities, permissions, roles, caller, tenant, clients, tokens, securityEvents, session, signIn, endpoints, commands, channels, dependencies, pages, algorithms, decisions), the tests, the deployment (environments, configuration, release, rollback, migrations) and the commissioning (checks, sign-off). On disk it is a folder whose root file is specarch.yaml; each stage listed under 'stages' lives in a folder of that name, and a stage not listed may be written inside specarch.yaml itself. The validator merges the tree into one document that this schema describes. Field keywords come from JSON Schema, endpoint keywords from OpenAPI 3, event keywords from AsyncAPI. Keywords with no standard origin are marked 'SpecArch keyword' in their description. Every object rejects unknown keys; keys starting with 'x-' are allowed everywhere as extensions.

specarch.description: Meta-model version this file is written against. In 0.3 the name caller is reserved for the caller record wherever an expression's names come from, and, as in 0.2, a derived case no test covers is an error; a 0.1 or 0.2 file is read until 1.0, with one warning that the file is on an earlier version, and a 0.1 file's missing tests are warnings.

trustDomain.description: SpecArch keyword, in the identity module's root file. The URI that names the trust domain: the aud of every transaction token, and the base of every security event's identifier, <trustDomain>/events/<rule> (ADR-107, ADR-109).

stages.description: SpecArch keyword. The life-cycle stages this specification keeps in folders of their own, in life-cycle order. A listed stage has a folder of that name beside specarch.yaml and its sections live there; a stage that is not listed has no folder, and its sections, if any, are written in specarch.yaml. Only in specarch.yaml.

sources.description: SpecArch keyword. The external sources this specification rests on and cites: standards, regulations, documents, interviews, existing systems and external requirement sets, keyed by kebab-case name. A citation anywhere in the specification ('cites') names one of these, so a source's title, edition and URL are written once. Only in specarch.yaml.

stakeholders.description: SpecArch keyword. Who has an interest in the system (ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148:2018, 5.2.2), keyed by kebab-case role name, never a person's name.

needs.description: SpecArch keyword. Raw stakeholder needs as gathered, before they are turned into requirements (ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148:2018, 5.2.3 and 6.3), keyed by ID such as NEED-1.

requirements.description: SpecArch keyword. The requirements of the system (ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148:2018, 6.4), keyed by ID such as SA-1. Design elements name the requirements they satisfy under 'satisfies'; tests and commissioning checks name the ones they verify under 'verifies'.

glossary.description: SpecArch keyword. Terms of the domain and their meaning (ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148:2018, 9.2.3), keyed by the term as written.

assumptions.description: SpecArch keyword. What is taken to be true without proof, and would change the design if it turned out false (ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148:2018, 9.5.19), keyed by ID such as ASSUME-1.

constraints.description: SpecArch keyword. Limits on the solution that are not negotiable: technical, organisational, legal (ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148:2018, 9.6.16; arc42 section 2), keyed by ID such as CON-1. Not to be confused with an entity's data constraints.

enums.description: Named value sets, keyed by PascalCase name.

entities.description: Persistent things with identity, keyed by PascalCase name. Each entity becomes a table (or collection) and a schema component.

views.description: SpecArch keyword, after the SQL view. Read models keyed by PascalCase name: one row per record of an entity, carrying every field of it and the properties the view adds, fields read through its relations and counts of its related records. A view is never written.

schemas.description: OpenAPI's components.schemas. Value objects keyed by PascalCase name: data passed around but not stored, with no identity, such as a diagnostic, a summary or a token's claims. A schema has no key and no table; a request body, a response, a message or another schema may refer to it, and an entity may not.

permissions.description: SpecArch keyword. Named rights, keyed by dotted lower-case name such as 'loans.create'. Two names are reserved and declared here like any other, so that each says why: 'public', which an operation or page grants to everyone, including unauthenticated callers, and 'nobody', which closes a route on purpose, so that it stays in the contract and refuses every caller; no role grants either (ADR-096).

roles.description: SpecArch keyword. Roles a caller can hold, each listing the permissions it grants. A role grants nothing it does not list.

caller.description: SpecArch keyword. Who is making the call, as the service knows it once the session or token has been checked: one record with the properties of a value object, which a role's rows rule names as caller.<property>. A token's claims fill the properties of their names, and a session fills them at sign-in; how a running service carries them from the request to the query is the implementation file's (ADR-095).

tenant.description: SpecArch keyword. The tenant scope, said once: every role reaches only the rows of an entity carrying key whose key equals the caller's property, as if each role wrote the rows rule <key> == caller.<property> for it, unless the role writes its own rule for that entity; the entities listed under shared are read whole by every tenant. An entity that carries no key, is not shared and is not limited by a rule of its own on every role is an error, so that an entity left out is never reached whole (ADR-179).

clients.description: SpecArch keyword. The programs that call the system, keyed by the software_id of RFC 7591, the publisher's name for the software across its versions, in kebab-case: an application, where a person signs in, or a service, which calls on its own account with the roles it holds and a proof of its identity on each request, or carries a person's call. A client holds roles as a person does, so what it may do is said once, through permissions (ADR-096, ADR-106, ADR-110).

tokens.description: SpecArch keyword. The token formats the service issues and accepts, keyed by camelCase name: a JWT (RFC 7519, with the access-token profile of RFC 9068) or an opaque reference, with its lifetime, its signature algorithm, its claims as properties, checks over the claims, and whether it is the default every operation accepts. A claim fills the caller's property of the same name; a transaction token (the OAuth Transaction Tokens draft) rides in the Txn-Token header across a trust domain (ADR-097, ADR-108, ADR-109, ADR-111).

securityEvents.description: SpecArch keyword. Where the security event every refusal of a caller derives is written: store, the dependency that is the append-only store, and alarm, the dependency that is the alarm channel an event of severity high, or a repeat for one client, goes to as well. An event is a Security Event Token (RFC 8417) holding the rule, the severity, the operation, the client, the subject and the hash of the refused token, never the token; a specification with tokens and clients declares it (ADR-109).

separationOfDuties.description: SpecArch keyword. Sets of permissions one holder must never have together, after the static separation of duty of ANSI INCITS 359, keyed by kebab-case name. No role may grant cardinality or more of a set's permissions; the techspec lists the combinations of roles that together reach a set, as roles never to be given to one person.

session.description: SpecArch keyword. How a caller's signed-in session ends: 'idleTimeout', the time without a request after which it expires, and 'absoluteTimeout', the time after signing in after which it expires whatever the caller does; at least one of the two (OWASP Session Management Cheat Sheet). Once a session is declared, every operation, command and page whose permission is not 'public' gets the derived red case 'denied with expired session'.

signIn.description: SpecArch keyword. How a person signs in at an identity provider: OpenID Connect's authorisation code flow with PKCE, the provider a dependency of kind identityProvider, the application client the person signs in through, the callback operation of this system that takes the code and the state and calls the provider, the identity token it receives, and the operation the provider's back-channel logout calls. A page event navigate: signIn leaves the application for the provider. The provider's issuer, its discovery document and its keys, and the client's client_id, are the deployment's, in the implementation file (ADR-182).

middlewares.description: SpecArch keyword. The steps a request passes before an operation's handler runs, such as checking a session, a permission, a tenant or a rate, or writing an audit line, keyed by kebab-case name and declared once. An operation lists the ones it runs, in order, under middlewares. Which function of the code each one is belongs to the implementation file (bindings.http.middlewares).

handshakes.description: SpecArch keyword. The key exchanges a client performs before it may call the operations that travel in an encrypted envelope, keyed by camelCase name and declared once: the key agreement, the signature and the cipher the envelope uses, the operation that establishes one, how long one lives and how many envelopes it carries. An operation names the one it travels in under handshake. The bytes of the envelope on the wire belong to the implementation file's stack.

paths.description: OpenAPI keyword. HTTP endpoints keyed by path template.

commands.description: SpecArch keyword. Command-line commands, keyed by the words a user types after the program name, such as 'validate' or 'generate techspec'. A command is an interface like an HTTP operation: it names a permission (fail-closed) and lists its arguments, options, files and exit codes.

channels.description: AsyncAPI keyword. Event channels keyed by channel name (dotted lower-case). Each channel carries one or more messages; a message is an event.

dependencies.description: SpecArch keyword. External systems the operations call, keyed by camelCase name: a payment gateway, a directory, a ledger. Each has a time limit per call. An operation names the ones it calls under 'calls'; the validator derives the cases where one fails and where one does not answer in time.

jobs.description: SpecArch keyword. The work the system does on its own, keyed by camelCase name.

gateways.description: SpecArch keyword, after RFC 9110's gateway (section 3.7). The intermediaries that forward every request no operation under paths answers, whatever its method and path, as received, to the service a claim of the verified bearer token names, keyed by camelCase name: the token verified, the claim read, the dependency each value of it selects, the dependencies called besides, the middlewares run and the refusals the gateway answers itself. A gateway names no permission: it decides nothing, and the service it forwards to checks the permission of every path it serves (ADR-141).

workflows.description: SpecArch keyword, a sequential subset of BPMN 2.0. Requests that finish later, after people approve them, keyed by kebab-case name: the operation that starts each, answering 202, the entity that holds the request while it waits, and its approval and operation steps in order. The person who made a request never approves it. A workflow is a test subject.

errors.description: SpecArch keyword. The catalogue of problem types the operations answer with, keyed by kebab-case name. Every 4xx and 5xx response is an RFC 9457 problem document and names its type under problem.

pages.description: SpecArch keyword. Screens, keyed by kebab-case name.

menus.description: SpecArch keyword. The navigation: a tree of entries whose leaves name pages, keyed by camelCase name. A leaf is shown to who has the page's permission.

flows.description: SpecArch keyword, after the navigation flows of OMG's IFML. Tasks a person does across pages, keyed by kebab-case name: who does it and each step, a page and the event on it that leads to the next step's page. A flow is a test subject.

accessibility.description: SpecArch keyword. The accessibility the user interface conforms to, by the standard and its level. With it, the validator checks what the design decides: a title for every field a page shows and a distinct label for every action of a page.

standard.description: WCAG 2.2, the W3C Recommendation of October 2023.

level.description: The conformance level; AA is what most laws ask for.

theme.description: SpecArch keyword. The visual design as design tokens in the format of the W3C Design Tokens Community Group, the modes that give a token another value, and the pairs of colours shown as text or controls on a background, whose contrast the validator checks against WCAG 2.2. How a token becomes code is the stack's.

modes.description: Other modes, such as dark, keyed by camelCase name: each gives tokens, by path, another value. The tokens' own values are the default mode.

algorithms.description: SpecArch keyword. Computations that must be specified before they are written by hand, keyed by camelCase name.

tests.description: SpecArch keyword. Design tests: what must hold whatever the stack, in plain given, when and then sentences. Each test is about one subject (an operation, a command, a page, or an entity's constraint or transition), has a level (system or acceptance) and is marked golden (the path that succeeds) or red (a path that fails). In a folder tree each test is a folder tests/<name>/ holding test.yaml and the scenario's own input and expected-output files. The validator derives the cases each subject needs from the rest of the specification and reports every one no test covers; see 'Tests' in docs/conventions.md.

decisions.description: SpecArch keyword. Architecture decision records, keyed by ID such as 'ADR-001'.

environments.description: SpecArch keyword. Where the system is installed, keyed by kebab-case name such as development, staging, production: what each is for and which one a release goes to next. Hosts, URLs and ports belong to an implementation file's deployments.

configuration.description: SpecArch keyword. The settings the system reads at run time, keyed by camelCase name: what each is, its type, and whether it is a secret. A secret's value is never written in a specification; the implementation file says where it comes from.

release.description: SpecArch keyword. How a new version is put into an environment, as ordered steps with a check for each (ISO/IEC/IEEE 12207:2017, 6.4.10 Transition process).

rollback.description: SpecArch keyword. How the previous version is restored when a release fails, as ordered steps with a check for each.

migrations.description: SpecArch keyword. Changes to stored data that a release carries, keyed by kebab-case name, each with its steps and how it is reversed. A migration that cannot be reversed says so in its description.

handover.description: SpecArch keyword. What the customer who runs an environment (runBy customer) receives to build, install and run it, and what stays whose responsibility. What another section already says, the settings, migrations, release, rollback, backup, restore, checks, sign-off and monitors, is read from there, never repeated here (ADR-129).

checks.description: SpecArch keyword. The checks run on the real installed system before it is handed over (the site acceptance test of IEC 62381:2024; ISO/IEC/IEEE 12207:2017, 6.4.11 Validation process), keyed by kebab-case name. Each names its kind, the environment it runs in and its steps. The results of each run are records, kept outside the specification; see 'Commissioning records' in docs/conventions.md.

signoff.description: SpecArch keyword. What must be true for the installed system to be accepted, and which roles sign.

monitors.description: SpecArch keyword. What is watched on the live system (ISO/IEC/IEEE 12207:2017, 6.4.12 Operation process), keyed by kebab-case name: each says what is measured, the objective it must meet, the environment it runs in and the requirements it verifies. The tool, the query and where an alert goes are implementation; the implementation file's deployments name them per monitor. Lives in the operation stage.

backup.description: SpecArch keyword. How the data of the live system is saved, as ordered steps with a check for each (ISO/IEC/IEEE 12207:2017, 6.4.12 Operation process).

restore.description: SpecArch keyword. How saved data is put back on the live system, as ordered steps with a check for each (ISO/IEC/IEEE 12207:2017, 6.4.12 Operation process).

questions.description: SpecArch keyword. The open questions: what the sources do not say and a stakeholder must decide or provide, keyed by ID such as Q-12. A question is written in the folder of the stage it is about, so every stage folder may hold questions; the validator merges them into one section and checks each sits in the stage of what it blocks. A question leaves the specification when it is answered; the decision that answered it names it under answers.

typeName.description: PascalCase identifier for an entity or enum.

memberName.description: camelCase identifier for a field, relation, algorithm or input.

idKey.description: SpecArch keyword. The ID of a requirement, need, assumption or constraint: an upper-case prefix of 2 to 16 letters or digits, a dash, and an ID, such as SA-1 or NEED-12.

duration.description: SpecArch keyword. A length of time as ISO 8601 writes it, in days, hours, minutes and seconds only and never zero: PT5S, PT30M, P1DT12H. Weeks, months and years are not allowed, because their length depends on the calendar, and a limit must mean the same every day.

questionId.description: SpecArch keyword. The ID of an open question: an upper-case prefix of 1 to 16 letters or digits, a dash, and an ID, such as Q-12 or OPEN-3.

requirementLink.description: SpecArch keyword. The ID of a requirement: one defined under 'requirements' in this specification, or one in an external requirement set declared under 'sources' with kind requirement-set, whose prefix is the set's prefix.

satisfies.description: SpecArch keyword. The requirements this element satisfies, by ID (the satisfy relation of ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148:2018, 6.5.1, and SysML). Every named design and deployment element carries it; fields, parameters, responses, actions and worked examples trace through the object that holds them. A requirement no element satisfies is reported by the validator.

verifies.description: SpecArch keyword. The requirements this test, commissioning check or monitor verifies, by ID (the verify relation of ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148:2018, 6.5.2). A requirement no test verifies is reported by the validator.

why.description: SpecArch keyword. The rationale in plain words: why this element is the way it is, what was concluded. Optional on every element; a document renders it as an Insight next to the element.

citation.description: SpecArch keyword. One citation: which source, where in it, and what it says here. A document renders it as a Note under the element's Insight.

source.description: The key of a source declared under 'sources' in specarch.yaml.

clause.description: The clause, section, page or question cited, as the source numbers it, such as '5.2.5' or 'Annex A'.

says.description: What the source says that applies here, in plain words: what it requires, recommends or reports.

citations.description: SpecArch keyword. The sources this element rests on, one citation each. Optional on every element.

origin.description: SpecArch keyword. How the element is known. stated: a source says it, and cites names the source and where in it. inferred: it was concluded from evidence (code, data, the source's silence), and why says from what. decided: a stakeholder settled it, answering a question or correcting the source, and decidedIn names the decision. An element without origin was written spec-first. What is not known at all is not an element with an origin but an open question under questions.

decidedIn.description: SpecArch keyword. With origin decided: the decision record that settled this element, such as ADR-021.

audience.description: SpecArch keyword. Who the element is for. internal: only the people who build and run the system, such as a note from inside the team or a requirement written as a proposal below the promises; specarch document --audience external leaves the element out and counts it, and every other document marks it. Left out, the element is for everyone. An element for everyone may not name an internal one through a $ref, a relation's target, a page's entity or a requirement's needs, since a document for everyone would then name what it may not show.

schemaRef.description: A JSON pointer into the specification, such as '#/entities/Member', '#/enums/LoanStatus', '#/views/LoanRow' or '#/schemas/Diagnostic', or into another specification through a dependency that names it, the dependency's name before the #, such as 'customerRegistry#/schemas/Address'. The pointer names the object wherever its file is in the tree.

entityTarget.description: SpecArch keyword. An entity of the specification by its name, such as Loan, or an entity of another specification through a dependency that names it, such as customerRegistry#/entities/Customer.

operationRef.description: SpecArch keyword. A name of the specification, such as listMembers, or an operation of another specification through a dependency that names it: the dependency's name, #/paths/, the path with each / written ~1 and each ~ written ~0, and the method, such as customerRegistry#/paths/~1customers/get.

info.description: OpenAPI keyword. What the system is. Only in specarch.yaml.

version.description: Version of the specification, semantic versioning.

name.description: SpecArch keyword. The specification's name in kebab case, such as customer-registry: what another specification's dependency gives as its specification, and the key an estate lists it under. Left out, no other specification can name it.

owners.description: SpecArch keyword. Teams or components accountable for the system, not people.

tracksOrigin.description: SpecArch keyword. true when the specification was built from sources and every element says how it is known: the validator then reports each element of a section that carries no origin (origin_missing, a warning).

roleNames.description: SpecArch keyword. How a role's name goes on the wire, in a token's roles claim and in the tables a permission check reads, when not as the specification names it. upper_snake: every role goes on the wire as its kebab-case name in upper case with each hyphen an underscore (desk-supervisor is DESK_SUPERVISOR); the validator refuses two roles that map to one wire name (wire_name). Left out, every role goes on the wire as written.

program.description: SpecArch keyword. The name a person types to run the system's command-line interface, such as specarch: the word before every command's words, which the user manual writes in each command's usage line. Left out, the manual writes each command by its words alone and says that this key names the program (ADR-165).

wireNames.description: SpecArch keyword. How the interface writes a property's name on the wire, when not as the specification names it. snake_case: every property of every entity, view, body, parameter schema and message payload goes on the wire in snake_case (loanedOn is loaned_on, userId and userID are user_id), and so do the property names an idiom gives, such as a list's paging; the validator refuses two properties of one object that map to one wire name (wire_name). A parameter's own name is written as it is on the wire and is not mapped. Left out, every name goes on the wire as written.

source.description: SpecArch keyword. One external source: where a requirement, a decision or any other element comes from, or what it cites.

kind.description: What the source is: a published standard; a law or regulation; a document (a book, a manual, a report, an internal document); an interview with a stakeholder; an existing system that was observed running; the source code of an existing system, read at one commit (the edition), whose citations name a file and line or a package and function as the clause; or an external tracker that links point into: a requirement set for requirement links, a change set for the change requests and a defect set for the defects that records name.

title.description: The title as the source itself gives it, such as 'ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148:2018 Systems and software engineering, Life cycle processes, Requirements engineering'.

edition.description: The edition, version or year, as the source gives it.

author.description: Who wrote or published it: a body, an organisation or a role, not a private person's name.

date.description: When an interview was held or a document was issued, as a quoted date.

url.description: Where the source can be read. For a requirement-set, change-set or defect-set, a URL template with {id} for one item.

givenOutside.description: SpecArch keyword. True when the system's owners gave this source to parties outside, such as a published interface, a manual handed to customers or a contract, so that a promise in it is not the project's alone to change. specarch merge asks a must question about an element only this source or only the code has.

language.description: SpecArch keyword. The language the source is written in, as a BCP 47 tag such as en or pt-BR: the language subtag and the subtags after it. specarch extract documents writes it when a vocabulary was named, so a reader of the tree knows which words were applied, and specarch merge reads a number of days in a requirement by that language's vocabulary. A source without it is read as English.

reading.description: SpecArch keyword. For kind code: how the code was read. printed when the running system printed what was read, such as a route table, a permission table or a catalogue dump; parsed when a parser read the source itself. specarch merge tells the two apart: an operation only the parsed reading declares is asked whether the running system has it, and one only the printed reading has is asked about as code the parser does not follow. A source merged from trees that read it both ways leaves it out.

prefix.description: For kind requirement-set, change-set or defect-set: the prefix of the IDs in that set, such as JIRA, so that a link JIRA-12 resolves to it. One tracker that holds several kinds is declared once per kind, and the prefixes may be the same.

clauses.description: SpecArch keyword. The outline of a document or of code: every section a document numbers or heads, or every package, folder or file of code, each once, so that specarch gaps can show which of them the specification cites and which produced nothing. A citation's clause falls under the longest listed clause it equals or starts with, followed by a dot, a colon, a slash or a space.

clause.description: The clause as citations name it: a section number or heading, or a path in the code.

title.description: The heading of the section, or what the code there does.

stakeholder.description: SpecArch keyword. One role with an interest in the system (ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148:2018, 5.2.2).

description.description: Who they are and what they do with the system.

concerns.description: What they need from the system or fear about it, one plain sentence each.

need.description: SpecArch keyword. One raw stakeholder need (ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148:2018, 6.3). A need is refined into one or more requirements, which name it under 'needs'.

statement.description: The need as the stakeholder would say it, in plain words.

stakeholders.description: The stakeholders who have this need, by key.

status.description: Where the need stands: proposed until the stakeholders confirm it, accepted when they do, rejected when it will not be met.

requirement.description: SpecArch keyword. One requirement with its attributes (ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148:2018, 5.2.8): what it asks, what kind it is, how important, where it stands, how it is accepted and verified, and which needs it comes from.

statement.description: The requirement as one verifiable sentence: who or what shall do what, under which condition (ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148:2018, 5.2.4 and 5.2.5).

kind.description: functional: what the system does; quality: how well (performance, usability, security, reliability); interface: how it connects to people and other systems; constraint: a limit on how it is built.

priority.description: must: the system is not acceptable without it; should: expected, but a release without it can be accepted; could: wanted when it costs little (MoSCoW, as used in DSDM).

status.description: proposed until the stakeholders agree to it, accepted when they do, rejected when it will not be met, retired when it no longer applies.

acceptance.description: The conditions under which the requirement counts as met, one verifiable sentence each; they are what the tests and commissioning checks show.

verification.description: How the requirement is shown to be met: inspection (looking at the item), analysis (calculation or model), demonstration (operating it), test (measuring it against defined criteria); the four methods of MIL-STD-961E and the INCOSE handbook.

needs.description: The needs this requirement refines, by ID.

harm.description: SpecArch keyword. What is at stake when the requirement is not met. A requirement with any harm is critical, and so is every derived test case of the elements that satisfy it; priority says whether a release may go without the requirement, not what a failure costs.

release.description: SpecArch keyword. The release the requirement is meant for, by version: records/releases/ must hold a release of that version, planned or released. The test plan groups the requirements by it.

ownedBy.description: SpecArch keyword. The stakeholder whose component fulfils the requirement, when it is not this system: the requirement stays in the specification as a promise, and the validator asks no element to satisfy it and no test, check or monitor to verify it. The same word names the owner of a mapping in an implementation file.

fulfilledBy.description: SpecArch keyword. With ownedBy: the requirement of another specification that fulfils this one, through a dependency that names that specification: the dependency's name, #/requirements/ and the ID, such as cardIssuer#/requirements/CI-4. It is resolved when that specification is given in the same run, and counted as unresolved otherwise.

definition.description: What the term means in this system, in plain words.

projectConstraint.description: SpecArch keyword. One constraint on the solution.

kind.description: technical: a platform, language or interface that is given; organisational: a team, process, budget or deadline; legal: a law, regulation or licence.

enum.description: JSON Schema keywords. A closed set of string values.

valueDescriptions.description: SpecArch keyword. Meaning of each value, keyed by value; JSON Schema has no per-value description.

field.description: JSON Schema keywords, a bounded subset. A field is either a scalar with a type, an array, a nested object, or a reference to an enum or entity.

oneOf.description: A type that also allows null, written as JSON Schema does: [string, 'null'].

title.description: JSON Schema's title: the label a person reads for the field, on a page and in a document.

format.description: The concrete type of the value, where the JSON type alone would leave it open. type says how the value is carried in JSON; format says what it is. An integer needs int32, int64 or uint64; a number needs double; a decimal is a string with format decimal, precision and scale; an int64 or uint64 that can exceed 2^53 is carried as a string with format int64 or uint64. See 'Types' in docs/conventions.md.

generatedDefault.description: SpecArch keyword. A default the database computes for each new record, from a closed set every stack shares: identifier, a new random UUID, on a field of format uuid; currentTime, the instant the record is written, on a field of format date-time. The type-rendering idiom's defaults part names the expression of each dialect. A field has default or generatedDefault, not both.

additionalProperties.description: JSON Schema keyword, on an object only. The members an object may have beyond the ones properties names, and the type of their values: a field, a map whose keys are any text and whose values are all of that type; true, any members of any value; false, no members beyond properties. Left out, the object says nothing of other members. An object with additionalProperties and no properties is a map; with both, the named members are fixed and the rest follow additionalProperties. Open is written true, never {}.

readOnly.description: Set by the system, never by a client (an ID, a timestamp).

precision.description: SpecArch keyword. Total digits of a decimal; required with format: decimal.

scale.description: SpecArch keyword. Digits after the decimal point; required with format: decimal.

mistakes.description: SpecArch keyword. How often users get this field wrong: frequent or rare. It replaces the default frequency of every derived test case about the field, which decides with the harm of the subject whether the case is written or left out.

sensitivity.description: SpecArch keyword. How sensitive the value is: public; internal, for staff only; personal, data about a person, masked in logs and shown only to who may see it; credential, a secret such as a password or a token, which no response carries unless the field is writeOnly. The masking per sensitivity is the pii-in-logs idiom.

storage.description: SpecArch keyword. On an entity's field that holds a schema: how the value is kept in the entity's row. columns: one column per part, named after the field and the part (address_street), the default for one value; json: one JSON column, the only way for a list of schemas.

atRest.description: SpecArch keyword. encrypted: the value is stored encrypted, so it cannot be searched, sorted or compared in storage unless lookup gives a way. The engine function and the key are the encrypted-column idiom.

lookup.description: SpecArch keyword. With atRest encrypted: hash, a salted hash kept beside the value, so the field can be a key, unique or filtered by equality.

properties.description: JSON Schema keyword. The entity's fields.

primaryKey.description: SpecArch keyword. Field or fields that identify a row.

relations.description: SpecArch keyword. Links to other entities, keyed by camelCase name.

constraints.description: SpecArch keyword. Rules the data must satisfy beyond a single field's own keywords, keyed by snake_case name (it becomes the database constraint name).

stateField.description: SpecArch keyword. The field whose enum values form this entity's state machine; transitions lists the allowed moves. Generators draw the state diagram from it.

transitions.description: SpecArch keyword. Allowed state changes of stateField.

audited.description: SpecArch keyword. true: every record carries who created and last changed it and when, set by the system and never by a caller: createdAt, createdBy, lastModifiedAt and lastModifiedBy, which the entity does not declare itself. The columns are the audit-fields idiom.

deletion.description: SpecArch keyword. soft: a delete marks the record deleted and keeps it; a deleted record is not listed and reads as not found. The flag, deleted, is not declared by the entity. The column is the soft-delete idiom.

target.description: The entity this relation points at, of this specification or, for many-to-one and one-to-one, of another through a dependency.

via.description: For many-to-one and one-to-one: the field on this entity that holds the foreign key. For one-to-many: the field on the target that points back. For many-to-many: the join entity.

onDelete.description: What happens to this side when the target row is deleted. Default restrict.

fields.description: For unique: the fields that together must be unique.

expression.description: For check: one expression in SpecArch's subset of CEL (docs/conventions.md) over the entity's fields, giving true or false.

where.description: For unique: one expression in SpecArch's subset of CEL over the entity's fields, giving true or false; the fields must be unique only among the records where it holds, as a partial unique index. generate sql writes it on the engines that have one and refuses on the others.

message.description: What a user is told when the constraint fails.

trigger.description: The operationId, command, channel message ('channel/Message') or algorithm that causes the move.

validity.description: SpecArch keyword. The fields that bound when a record is current: 'from', the date or instant from which it is valid, which may be left out, and 'until', the date or instant after which it is expired. Both name fields of this entity with the same format, date or date-time. A record used outside its validity is refused; the validator derives that case for every operation that takes one.

from.description: The field holding the date or instant from which the record is valid.

until.description: The field holding the date or instant after which the record is expired.

implies.description: SpecArch keyword. Permissions this one implies: a holder of it holds each of them too, and what they imply, transitively. A client depends on it, since a holder calls what an implied permission guards without being told of it. Every name is declared, none is public, and no permission implies itself through the list (the implies rule).

permissions.description: Permissions this role grants. Fail-closed: an empty list is not allowed; a role that grants nothing is left out.

rows.description: SpecArch keyword. The rows the role reaches, keyed by entity: one expression over the entity's fields and the caller's properties (caller.<property>), giving true or false, in the subset of docs/conventions.md. A holder reads and changes only the records it holds for; an entity not listed is reached whole; a caller holding several roles reaches the union of their rows, after PostgreSQL's permissive row security policies. A rows rule grants nothing: the permission a holder needs is still the role's (ADR-095).

through.description: SpecArch keyword. The clients a grant holds through, keyed by a permission the role grants, directly or by implies: the application the caller signed in through, or the client calling on its own account, must be one listed, checked at every hop against the token's client_id or tctx.application. A permission not listed holds through every client. Listing nobody is not written: to close the grant, drop the permission (ADR-106, ADR-108).

permissions.description: The permissions of the set, each declared and none of them public.

cardinality.description: How many of the set's permissions one holder may not reach: at least 2, at most the number the set names, and 2 when left out.

session.description: SpecArch keyword. The one session object of a specification.

idleTimeout.description: The time without a request after which the session expires.

absoluteTimeout.description: The time after signing in after which the session expires, whatever the caller does.

signIn.description: SpecArch keyword. The one sign-in flow through an identity provider of a specification (ADR-182).

kind.description: The protocol: oidc, OpenID Connect Core 1.0.

provider.description: The dependency, of kind identityProvider, the person signs in at and the callback calls to exchange the code.

client.description: The client, of kind application, the person signs in through: the identity token's aud is its client_id, which the deployment gives (deployments.<environment>.clients.<name>.clientId).

flow.description: The grant: authorizationCode, the authorisation code flow of RFC 6749, section 4.1, and OpenID Connect Core, section 3.1.

pkce.description: Proof Key for Code Exchange (RFC 7636) with the S256 method, which RFC 9700, section 2.1.1, asks of every client.

callback.description: operationId of the operation of this system the provider sends the person back to: a GET taking code and state as required query parameters, naming the provider under calls.

identityToken.description: The token, under tokens, the provider returns from the exchange: a JWT declaring iss, aud and nonce, with no const or enum on iss or aud, since the issuer and the client_id are the deployment's.

logout.description: What ends a session from the provider's side.

backChannel.description: operationId of the operation the provider calls when the person signs out there (OpenID Connect Back-Channel Logout 1.0), which only declared service clients may call.

pathItem.description: OpenAPI keyword. The operations on one path.

operation.description: OpenAPI keywords plus the SpecArch 'permission'. An operation without a permission is invalid: access is fail-closed.

permission.description: SpecArch keyword. The one permission a caller must hold. Use 'public' for an endpoint open to everyone, and 'nobody' for a route that exists and is closed to everyone on purpose, which stays in the contract and refuses every caller (ADR-096).

callers.description: SpecArch keyword. Who may call: the explicit subset, people (anyone signed in; which people is the roles' business) and clients by name, in any order. Left out, it is [people]: a client is refused. A client listed must hold a role that grants the permission, and a service with no roles cannot be listed (ADR-110). There is no all: a client added later is admitted only once someone writes it here.

token.description: SpecArch keyword. The token this operation accepts, when it is not the default: a name under tokens (ADR-097).

via.description: SpecArch keyword. The immediate callers of this operation on a person's behalf: the services that call it with the transaction token, each with a workload-identity proof. Required on an operation accepting a transaction token or a token declaring act, refused elsewhere; every caller is written out, since a wildcard would admit a hop added later without anyone writing it (ADR-111).

middlewares.description: SpecArch keyword. The middlewares the operation runs before its handler, in the order they run, by their names under middlewares, one that runs twice named twice; an empty list says it runs none.

emits.description: SpecArch keyword. Channel messages this operation publishes, as 'channel/Message'.

calls.description: SpecArch keyword. The dependencies this operation calls, by their names under 'dependencies'. An entry may name one operation of a dependency that is another specification, as customerRegistry#/paths/~1customers/get.

idempotencyKey.description: SpecArch keyword. The name of a header parameter of this operation by which a repeated request is told from a new one: a request repeated with the same key is answered as the first was and has no second effect, and a different request with a key already used is refused. Only on a method that is not idempotent by itself (RFC 9110, 9.2.2): post or patch.

handshake.description: SpecArch keyword. The handshake, by its name under handshakes, whose envelope this operation's request travels in, and its response too unless the operation streams a download, which leaves the envelope. A client establishes the handshake first, through the operation the handshake names under establishedBy.

stream.description: SpecArch keyword. The operation carries a file as a stream rather than a body read whole: an upload reads the request body from its first byte to its last as it arrives, a download writes the response body the same way. The media type and that it is binary stay where OpenAPI puts them, in the request body of an upload and the success response of a download, as a string of format binary. An upload's parameters, which cannot travel in a body that is the file, go under parameters. The largest upload is limits.maxRequestBytes, the largest download limits.maxResponseBytes.

direction.description: upload: the request body is the file. download: the success response's body is the file.

parameters.description: SpecArch keyword. An upload's parameters, sent together as one JSON object in one header of the request beside the file: a schema of type object with its properties, or a $ref to a schema or an entity, as a request body's. Allowed beside direction upload only. Which header carries them is the stack's (ADR-162).

algorithm.description: SpecArch keyword. The algorithm this operation runs, if any.

enabledBy.description: SpecArch keyword. The boolean setting of configuration that switches this on: while the setting is false it is refused as not available. The derived case 'disabled by <setting>' checks it.

problem.description: SpecArch keyword. The problem type this response answers with, by its name under errors. Once the specification declares errors, every 4xx and 5xx response names one.

content.description: OpenAPI keyword. Media type to schema.

guard.description: SpecArch keyword. What is checked together with a data change: the entity it writes, a precondition over that entity's fields that must hold on the records as they are at the moment of the change, and the exact number of records it changes. The checks run with the change itself, so a writer who read a record before another writer changed it is refused rather than overwriting the other's change, and a change that would touch more records than expected is refused as a whole. The validator derives the cases 'guard precondition fails' and 'concurrent write'.

entity.description: The entity whose records the change writes.

precondition.description: One expression in SpecArch's subset of CEL (docs/conventions.md) over the entity's fields, giving true or false, that must hold on each record as it is when the change is made.

recordsChanged.description: The exact number of records of the entity the change writes.

writes.description: SpecArch keyword. What the change writes, when no keyword of the entry says it: set, the fields it sets, or delete, that it deletes the records (sets the soft-delete flag of an entity deleted softly). A transition the entry triggers still moves the state field, and set adds to it; a PUT of the entity by one path parameter and a DELETE by one path parameter already say what they write, so writes on one is an error. specarch-gen-scripts writes the guarded script from it (ADR-168).

set.description: The fields the change sets, each with its value: one expression in SpecArch's subset of CEL (docs/conventions.md) that is a literal of the field's type (a string in double quotes, a number, true, false, or null for a field that is not required or whose type allows null) or given, the value the operator gives when running the change. Neither the key nor the state field is set here: a key names the record, and a state is moved by a transition.

delete.description: The change deletes the records, or sets their soft-delete flag when the entity is deleted softly.

carriedBy.description: SpecArch keyword. The dependencies, by their keys under dependencies, that carry the channel: the broker it lives on, or the system that receives its messages directly. Left out, the channel is this system's own (ADR-134).

dependency.description: SpecArch keyword. One external system an operation calls.

timeout.description: The time limit of one call: after it, the call is given up and the operation answers as it does when the dependency fails.

kind.description: SpecArch keyword. What the dependency is: system, a software system with an interface this one calls; database, a data store another party keeps that this system reads or writes directly; messageBroker, a broker that carries channels; fileStore, a file exchange or object store; identityProvider, the issuer of the tokens this system accepts. Left out, it is system. It sets the dependency's shape in the context diagram (ADR-134).

protocol.description: AsyncAPI keyword, from its server object: how the dependency is reached, as a lowercase URI scheme name (RFC 3986, 3.1), such as https, grpc, amqp, kafka, mqtt, postgresql, sftp or smtp. Kept open, as AsyncAPI keeps it (ADR-134).

specification.description: SpecArch keyword. When the dependency is a system specified on its own: that specification's name, its info.name. Its elements are then named from this specification as <dependency>#/<pointer>, in a $ref, a relation's target, a picker's or a list page's source, and calls.

version.description: SpecArch keyword. The info.version of the other specification that the references were written against; the validator compares it when that specification is given.

page.description: SpecArch keyword. A screen of one of six kinds: a list, a form or a view of an entity's records, a task that submits to an operation without loading a record, a content page of headings, text, images and links that loads and submits nothing, or a custom page, a screen the project builds by hand, for which the generators write the route, the guard and the menu entry. Generators map it onto the target project's component library.

route.description: Client-side route; {param} marks a path parameter.

entity.description: The entity whose records a list, form or view shows. A task page and a content page show none and leave it out; a custom page may name the entity whose records its screen works on. A list page whose source is a list of another specification names that list's entity the same way, as customerRegistry#/entities/Customer.

source.description: operationId that loads the page's data. Required for list and view; a form that creates a new row has nothing to load and leaves it out, a form that edits an existing row names the operation that loads it. A list page may name a list of another specification through a dependency, as customerRegistry#/paths/~1customers/get, with its entity named the same way.

submit.description: For a form or a task: operationId that receives it. A task's fields are properties of its request body.

columns.description: For a list: fields shown, in order.

compactColumns.description: For a list: the columns a compact screen keeps, in order. What compact means in points or pixels, and how the row is laid out, is the stack's.

fields.description: For a form or view: fields of its entity shown, in order. For a task: properties of the submit operation's request body, every required one among them.

sections.description: For a form or a view, in place of fields: its fields in groups, each with a title, in the order a person reads them, which is the focus order (WCAG 2.2, 2.4.3). How groups sit on a screen is the stack's.

blocks.description: For a content page: what it shows under its title, in the order a person reads them, which is the reading and focus order (WCAG 2.2, 1.3.2 and 2.4.3). Every text of a block is a string key of the page, translated as its title is. How blocks sit on a screen is the stack's.

childRows.description: For a form: the records of a one-to-many relation of its entity, edited as rows under it, one entry per relation, in the order a person reads them.

filters.description: For a list: fields the user can filter on.

onSubmitted.description: For a form: where a successful submission leads. For a task: what each success the submit operation answers leads to, keyed by its response status. A page that submits to a workflow's trigger acts on the 202 answer, a form with its one event and a task under 202, with the message that says the request waits for approval: the page's pending state.

onSelect.description: For a list: where selecting a row leads.

pickers.description: For a form: the fields that hold the key of another entity's record, keyed by field, each picked from a list of that record. The field is the via of a many-to-one relation of the page's entity, which names the record's entity.

fieldConditions.description: For a form or a view: when a field it shows is read-only or hidden, keyed by field. Which mode a page is in, create, edit or view, is the page itself: a form without source creates, a form with one edits, and a view shows.

checks.description: For a form or a task: rules across the fields it shows, checked before it is sent, keyed in kebab case. On a task the fields are properties of the request body it sends.

enteredTwice.description: For a form or a task: fields a person types twice, so a mistake shows before it is sent. The second entry is compared and never sent.

enabledBy.description: SpecArch keyword. The boolean setting of configuration that switches this on: while the setting is false it is refused as not available. The derived case 'disabled by <setting>' checks it.

target.description: A page name for navigate, an operationId for operation.

permission.description: Shown only to callers holding it; defaults to the page's permission.

confirm.description: Question asked before an operation runs.

reason.description: For an operation with confirm: the property of its request body that carries the reason the person gives in the confirmation, a string the body requires.

when.description: An expression over the fields of the record the action is on, a row of a list or the record a view or an edit form shows, in the expression subset; the action is offered only while it is true.

then.description: For an operation: where it leads once it succeeds.

with.description: For navigate on a list: the route parameters of the page it opens, each from a field of the row it is on, exactly the parameters that page's route takes. A list's action that opens a page whose route takes a parameter is offered on each row, while its when holds; one whose page takes none is a button of the list's toolbar.

pageEvent.description: SpecArch keyword, after the navigation flow of OMG's IFML. Where an event of a page leads: to another page with the route parameters it needs, and with a message announced to the person (WCAG 2.2, 4.1.3). Geometry and animation are a stack's.

navigate.description: The page the event leads to, or signIn, the reserved word for the identity provider's sign-in (ADR-182): the one event that leaves the application, on a task page's answer or an action's then, with no with and no message.

with.description: The route parameters of the page navigated to, each from a field of this page's entity: the record submitted, selected or acted on. On a task page, each from a property of the body of the response the event follows.

message.description: A status message, a full sentence, announced without moving focus.

inbox.description: SpecArch keyword. For a list: the workflow and approval step it is the inbox of, listing the requests that wait there. The list shows the workflow's subject and checks the step's permission.

workflow.description: The workflow, by its name under workflows.

step.description: The approval step of that workflow whose requests the list shows.

statusEvents.description: SpecArch keyword. What a task page does on each success its submit operation answers, keyed by the response status, each one the operation declares. A problem the operation answers is shown under the page's failed states, not here.

actor.description: The role that does the task; it must be allowed to open every page on the way.

steps.description: The pages in order, each with the event that leads to the next one's page.

event.description: What the person does on it: selects a row of a list, submits a form, or takes an action.

action.description: For event action: the label of the action.

trigger.description: The operationId that starts the workflow. Its request body is the workflow's form, and it answers 202: the request is accepted and waits.

subject.description: The entity that holds the request while it waits.

steps.description: The steps in order, after BPMN 2.0: an approval is a user task with its potential owners and a timer, an operation a service task. A refusal at an approval ends the request.

emits.description: The channel messages the workflow publishes when it ends, approved or refused, as channel/Message, so a page waiting on it knows how the end is announced.

name.description: The step's name, unique in the workflow.

kind.description: approval: people with the permission approve or refuse the request; operation: the system calls an operation once every approval before it has passed.

approvers.description: For an approval: the roles that may approve, each granting the permission.

permission.description: For an approval: the permission the approval checks; never the trigger's.

deadline.description: For an approval: how long the request waits for an answer.

onDeadline.description: For an approval: what the deadline does when it passes. refuse ends the request; escalate moves it to the later approval step named under escalateTo.

escalateTo.description: With onDeadline escalate: the later approval step the request moves to.

operation.description: For an operation step: the operationId the system calls.

pageStates.description: SpecArch keyword. What a page shows in each state but its content: empty and filtered empty for a list, and failed per problem type it can meet. Loading and submitting have no text of their own, and a stack draws them its way. Without states, a stack shows its own.

empty.description: For a list: what it shows when there are no records.

filteredEmpty.description: For a list with filters: what it shows when no record matches them.

failed.description: What the page shows when an operation it calls fails, keyed by problem type, or default for every problem type not named.

message.description: A full sentence the person reads, and a screen reader announces (WCAG 2.2, 3.3.1 and 4.1.3).

field.description: For a failed state of a form: the field the problem is about, so the message shows beside it.

picker.description: SpecArch keyword. A field picked from a list of the records it may hold the key of.

source.description: operationId of the list the record is picked from, an operation whose listOf names the relation's target; or such an operation of another specification through a dependency, as customerRegistry#/paths/~1customers/get.

shows.description: The fields of the picked record a person reads to choose it, in order.

fills.description: Other fields of the form set from the picked record: the form's field, then the record's field of the same type.

fieldCondition.description: SpecArch keyword. When a field a page shows is read-only or hidden. Each expression is over the fields of the record, in the expression subset.

readOnly.description: For a form: the field is shown and never changed on this page.

readOnlyWhen.description: For a form: the field is shown and not changed while this is true.

hiddenWhen.description: The field is not shown while this is true.

formCheck.description: SpecArch keyword. A rule across a form's fields, an expression over the fields it shows that must be true before it is sent.

message.description: A full sentence the person reads when the rule does not hold.

field.description: The field the message shows beside.

contentBlock.description: SpecArch keyword. One block of a content page: a heading, a paragraph of text, an image or a link, exactly one of them.

heading.description: A heading over the blocks after it. The page's title is the heading of level 1.

level.description: Its level, 1 to 6, as HTML's h1 to h6; a level is at most one below the heading before it (WCAG 2.2, 1.3.1).

image.description: An image the project serves at path, beside the screens; the generator copies nothing and checks no file.

path.description: Where the image is served, relative to the site's root, as images/studio.jpg: no scheme, no leading / or \, no . or .. folder and no ?, #, % or space, so it stays on the site.

alternativeText.description: What the image shows, for who cannot see it (WCAG 2.2, 1.1.1). Required once the specification names its accessibility target.

link.description: A link to a page of the specification, whose route takes no parameter, or to an address outside it.

href.description: An address outside the specification: https, http or mailto only, so that no link runs script (javascript:) or carries a document (data:).

label.description: The link's text, which says where it leads (WCAG 2.2, 2.4.4). Required once the specification names its accessibility target.

childRows.description: SpecArch keyword. The records of one relation of a form's entity, edited as rows under the form: added, changed and removed with it. Each row is validated by the target entity's own schema.

relation.description: A one-to-many relation of the form's entity; its target is the entity of each row.

fields.description: The fields of the relation's target shown in each row, in order.

maximum.description: The most rows the form holds, loaded and new together; a row past it is refused.

lockLoadedRows.description: true: the rows loaded with the record are shown and cannot be changed or removed; only rows added on the form change.

tokenGroup.description: A group of design tokens, after the W3C Design Tokens Community Group's Format Module 2025.10: $type gives the type of every token it holds that does not give its own, and every other key is a token, which has a $value, or a group.

$extensions.description: The format's extensions, keyed by the reverse domain of the tool that writes them; SpecArch keeps them and reads none.

$deprecated.description: The format's deprecation: true, or a sentence saying what to use instead.

designToken.description: A design token: its $value, of its type or an alias of another token written {group.token}, its $type when no group gives it and it is not an alias, a $description, and the format's $extensions and $deprecated.

$extensions.description: The format's extensions, keyed by the reverse domain of the tool that writes them; SpecArch keeps them and reads none.

$deprecated.description: The format's deprecation: true, or a sentence saying what to use instead.

text.description: The colour token used as text or as the part of a control, by its path.

background.description: The colour token it is shown on.

use.description: text asks 4.5:1 at AA (1.4.3) and 7:1 at AAA (1.4.6); largeText, 18 point or 14 point bold, asks 3:1 and 4.5:1; control, the parts of a control and graphics, asks 3:1 (1.4.11).

algorithm.description: SpecArch keyword. All three of formula, examples and pseudocode are required; the examples become test cases.

formula.description: The computation as one expression in SpecArch's subset of CEL (docs/conventions.md). It is type-checked against the inputs' declared types, with no implicit conversion, and its result must have the output's type. The validator evaluates it on every worked example.

note.description: Why this case matters or how the number was reached.

decision.description: SpecArch keyword. A short architecture decision record: the context (what was true and at stake), the decision, its consequences, and under 'why' the reasoning that led from the one to the other.

answers.description: SpecArch keyword. The open questions this decision answers, by ID. The questions themselves are removed from the specification once answered, so these IDs are text, not references; the validator refuses an accepted decision that answers a question still present.

opens.description: SpecArch keyword. The open questions this decision raised, by ID: what it answered only in part, or what it made necessary to ask. Each is a question of the specification while it is open, and is named under answers by a later decision once it is answered; a decision does not open a question it answers. specarch gaps shows each such question under the decision that opened it and the questions that decision answered.

decidedBy.description: SpecArch keyword. The stakeholder who decided, by key; a role, never a person. Required when the decision answers questions.

question.description: SpecArch keyword. One open question: something the sources do not say and a stakeholder must decide or provide. ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148:2018 (5.2.6) says a complete set of requirements holds no 'to be defined' clause and that resolving them is iterative within a time set by risk; IEEE Std 830-1998 (4.3.3) says such an item carries why it is open, what must be done, who is responsible and by when. A question is the one licence for an element to be incomplete: a required key may be missing exactly where a must question says it is unknown.
What is asked, as one plain question.

kind.description: decision: the stakeholder decides; material: the stakeholder provides something to read, such as a document, a file, a screenshot or a record.

priority.description: must: what it blocks is not defined, and nothing that reads it can be generated; should: what it blocks is written as inferred and the stakeholder should confirm it before it is built on; could: the answer would improve the specification, but nothing waits for it.

certainty.description: SpecArch keyword. On a question a reader asks about code it checked against the specification: certain when the code, as written, cannot work or disagrees with the specification; suspected when the reader sees the shape of a fault that a run or a person must confirm. Left out on every other question.

blocks.description: What cannot be final until the question is answered: a stage name, a section name, or a pointer to an element (#/entities/Loan, #/paths/~1loans/post) or to one key of it (#/requirements/BR-3/priority). A must question covers the required keys missing at or under an element pointer, and the one key of a key pointer.

decidedBy.description: The stakeholder who decides or provides, by key; a role, never a person.

options.description: For a decision with a known set of answers: the answers, two or more, so that the question can be put as a choice.

names.description: For a question that blocks one key a reader left out: the name the source gives there, which only another surface declares, such as the operation a workflow's trigger names. The key is left out until the name resolves; specarch merge writes it at the key and removes the question once the merged specification declares an element of that name.

commandName.description: SpecArch keyword. One or more kebab-case words separated by single spaces, as typed after the program name.

command.description: SpecArch keyword. One command of a command-line interface. Design only: how the arguments are parsed and which library does it belong in an implementation file.

permission.description: SpecArch keyword. The one permission a caller must hold. Use 'public' for an endpoint open to everyone, and 'nobody' for a route that exists and is closed to everyone on purpose, which stays in the contract and refuses every caller (ADR-096).

callers.description: SpecArch keyword. Who may call: the explicit subset, people (anyone signed in; which people is the roles' business) and clients by name, in any order. Left out, it is [people]: a client is refused. A client listed must hold a role that grants the permission, and a service with no roles cannot be listed (ADR-110). There is no all: a client added later is admitted only once someone writes it here.

options.description: Named options, keyed by the long name without its leading dashes.

reads.description: Files and folders the command reads.

writes.description: Files and folders the command writes. A command that writes nothing leaves this out.

standardOutput.description: What the command prints on standard output.

standardError.description: What the command prints on standard error.

exitCodes.description: Every exit status the command can return, keyed by number. Status 0 is required.

remedies.description: SpecArch keyword. What the person who ran the command does next after it exits with a status, in their words, keyed by a status exitCodes lists other than 0; the user manual writes it beside that status. Plain text with no reference in it (ADR-165).

algorithm.description: SpecArch keyword. The algorithm this command runs, if any.

enabledBy.description: SpecArch keyword. The boolean setting of configuration that switches this on: while the setting is false it is refused as not available. The derived case 'disabled by <setting>' checks it.

repeatable.description: The argument takes one or more values; only the last argument may.

path.description: A path or a pattern; {name} marks a part taken from an argument or option.

stackSpecificKey.description: Extension keys that belong to one implementation, not to the design: code-generator settings, a language or framework binding, servers, hosts, ports and deployments. They go in a SpecArch Implementation File (*.specarch-implementation.yaml), never in a design file. See 'Design and implementation' in docs/conventions.md.

test.description: SpecArch keyword. One test scenario. Exactly one subject: operation, command, page, job, flow, workflow, requirement, or entity, alone for its state machine or with one constraint or transition. In a folder tree it is the content of tests/<name>/test.yaml.

job.description: The job the test is about.

gateway.description: The gateway the test is about (ADR-141).

workflow.description: The workflow the test is about.

requirement.description: The requirement whose acceptance criteria the test shows met: its cases are 'acceptance 1', 'acceptance 2' and so on, one per criterion, and the test is usually level acceptance.

entity.description: The entity under test: alone, its state machine, whose cases are its paths from an initial to a terminal state such as 'open to overdue to returned'; with constraint or transition, that one.

constraint.description: With entity: the constraint under test.

transition.description: With entity: the transition under test.

scenario.description: golden for the path that succeeds, red for a path that fails.

level.description: system: the test exercises the system through its interfaces as a client would; acceptance: it shows a stakeholder that a requirement is met, so it names one under 'verifies'. Unit and integration tests belong to an implementation file's suites. The levels are those of ISO/IEC/IEEE 29119-1.

given.description: The state before, in plain words.

fixture.description: SpecArch keyword. The state before the test, for a generator: caller, the role making the call or public, as a word or as an object with the role and the caller's properties, and records that exist, by entity name.

oneOf.description: The role making the call, or public.
The role making the call under role, or public, and a value for each property of the caller the test needs, by its name.

input.description: SpecArch keyword. What the call carries, for a generator: an operation's parameters and body fields by name; a command's arguments and options; a page's route parameters and action, the label of one of its actions.

expect.description: SpecArch keyword. The outcome, for a generator: an operation's status and the body fields that matter; a command's exit and lines of standardOutput; the state after, as records by entity name; and emits, the messages published, or emitsNothing.

status.description: One of the operation's response statuses.

body.description: Fields of the entity the response returns, with their values.

exit.description: One of the command's exit codes.

standardOutput.description: Lines the command prints, in order.

covers.description: The derived cases this test covers, written exactly as the validator names them, such as 'missing memberId'.

notApplicable.description: Instead of given, when and then: why the derived cases in covers do not apply to this subject. Only with a written reason.

step.description: SpecArch keyword. One step of a procedure or a check.

name.description: A short name for the step, such as 'Tag the release'.

action.description: What is done, in plain words. The exact command belongs to the implementation file.

check.description: How the person running it knows the step worked.

procedure.description: SpecArch keyword. An ordered procedure: a release or a rollback.

environment.description: SpecArch keyword. One environment the system is installed in.

description.description: What the environment is for and who uses it.

promotesTo.description: The environment a release goes to after it has passed here, by key. The last environment leaves it out.

runBy.description: SpecArch keyword. Who installs and runs the environment. vendor: the team that builds the system. customer: the party that takes the system builds, installs and runs it on hosts of its own, from the handover; the specification then needs handover, release and rollback, and the implementation file's deployment of it needs build, method and infrastructure. Left out, the vendor runs it (ADR-129).

handover.description: SpecArch keyword. What the customer who runs an environment receives to build, install and run it, and what stays whose responsibility.

description.description: The handover in plain words: what is handed over, when, and how the customer takes it.

to.description: The stakeholder who receives the handover, by key; a role, never a person.

source.description: How the source of a release reaches the customer, such as a tagged release of the repository that the customer imports into a repository of its own.

responsibilities.description: What stays whose responsibility once the system is handed over, one plain sentence each.

customer.description: What the customer is responsible for: the hosts, their patching, backups, monitoring, and so on.

vendor.description: What the vendor stays responsible for: the source of each release, fixes for reported defects, and so on.

description.description: What the setting controls and where its value comes from.

secret.description: True when the value must never be written in a specification or a document: a password, a key, a token. The validator refuses a default or a deployment value for a secret.

migration.description: SpecArch keyword. One data migration a release carries.

rollback.description: How the data change is reversed. Left out only when the description says why it cannot be.

check.description: SpecArch keyword. One commissioning check on the installed system.

kind.description: smoke: the installed system starts and answers; end-to-end: a whole use goes through on the real infrastructure; performance: it meets its load and time targets; security: access and exposure are as designed; data: the data it holds or migrated is right.

environment.description: The environment the check runs in, by key.

monitor.description: SpecArch keyword. One monitor of the live system.

description.description: What is measured, in plain words.

environment.description: The environment the monitor watches, by key.

objective.description: What the measurement must stay within, as one verifiable sentence, such as 'nine calls in ten answer within 300 ms over a day'.

response.description: SpecArch keyword. What the operator does when the objective is missed, as steps with a check for each. The operations guide writes it under the monitor (ADR-160).

signoff.description: SpecArch keyword. The acceptance of the installed system.

criteria.description: What must be true for the system to be accepted, one plain sentence each.

signers.description: The roles that sign the acceptance, never people's names.

testRecords.description: SpecArch keyword. Records by entity name: each a list of records, each naming the fields that matter with values of the field's type.

listOf.description: SpecArch keyword. The operation answers a page of an entity's records, or of a view's rows: which fields a free-text search covers, which may be filtered and sorted by, and the page size. A client must know the lists, and a request outside them is refused, never ignored. The parameter names and the answer's envelope are the paginated-list idiom.

view.description: The view listed, in place of an entity; the whitelists then name the view's fields.

searchable.description: The fields a free-text search matches.

filterable.description: The fields a filter may name.

sortable.description: The fields the list may be sorted by.

pageSize.description: How many records a page holds.

maximum.description: The largest page a request may ask for; above it the request is refused.

limits.description: SpecArch keyword. Limits a client must keep to, and the largest answer it must be ready for: the largest request body, the largest response body of a download stream, and how many requests are taken in a time. The runtime side is the rate-limit idiom.

maxRequestBytes.description: The largest request body, in bytes; a larger one is refused.

maxResponseBytes.description: The largest response body, in bytes, of an operation that streams a download; the system answers no larger file, and a client need be ready for no more. Only beside stream: {direction: download}.

rate.description: How many requests one caller may make in a time, and how many at once above that.

problemType.description: SpecArch keyword. One kind of problem an operation answers with, in the shape of RFC 9457, Problem Details for HTTP APIs: its HTTP status, a short title that does not change between occurrences, and the condition under which it is answered.

remedy.description: SpecArch keyword. What the person who meets the problem does next, in their words, such as 'ask the member to return a copy first'. The user manual writes it beside the message each page shows for the problem (ADR-160).

type.description: The problem type's URI, when it is not derived from the name.

middleware.description: SpecArch keyword. One step a request passes before an operation's handler runs: what it checks or does, and the refusals it answers when the check fails, each with its status and the problem type it names.

refusals.description: The answers the step gives in place of the handler's, in the order it checks.

problem.description: The problem type under errors that the refusal names.

handshake.description: SpecArch keyword. One key exchange between a client and the system, after which the client's requests and the system's answers on the operations that name it travel in an envelope: encrypted with the cipher under a key both derive by the key agreement, and signed by each side's signature key, so that neither a proxy nor the transport sees or alters a body. What a client must do is what this declares; the bytes on the wire belong to the stack.

keyAgreement.description: The key agreement both sides run, by its name in RFC 7748: x25519 or x448. Each side sends its public key, and both derive the same shared secret.

signature.description: The signature each side puts on the envelope it sends, by its name in RFC 8032: ed25519 or ed448. The public key travels with the key agreement's, so the receiver verifies who sealed the envelope.
