cipher.description: The cipher the envelope is encrypted with, under the key the key agreement gives, by its OpenSSL name: aes-256-cbc, aes-256-gcm or chacha20-poly1305.

establishedBy.description: The operationId of the operation a client calls to perform the exchange: it sends its public keys in the request and receives the system's, with an index that names the handshake in every envelope after. That operation travels in no envelope itself.

lifetime.description: How long a handshake is accepted after it is established; an envelope under one older than this is refused and the client establishes a new one. Left out, a handshake does not expire by time.

uses.description: How many envelopes one handshake carries before the client must establish a new one: 1 for a handshake used once, as a pre-key is. Left out, a handshake carries any number within its lifetime.

job.description: SpecArch keyword. Work the system does on its own: on a schedule, at an interval, or for each message it consumes. It acts as a role, reads and writes entities, may call dependencies and publish messages, and retries a failed item a bounded number of times.

trigger.description: What starts the job: exactly one of schedule, a cron expression of five fields in UTC; every, a duration between runs; consumes, the channel/Message it handles one at a time.

role.description: The role the job acts as; its permissions are what the job may do.

calls.description: The dependencies the job calls. An entry may name one operation of a dependency that is another specification, as customerRegistry#/paths/~1customers/get.

emits.description: The messages the job publishes, as channel/Message.

retries.description: How often a failed item is tried again, and what becomes of it after the last try: deadLetter keeps it apart for a person, as the job's deadLetter says, discard drops it.

deadLetter.description: SpecArch keyword. What becomes of an item the job keeps apart after its last try, when retries says deadLetter: the role whose people handle it, where it is kept and how to look at it, and the steps to try it again or discard it, each with a check. The operations guide writes it under the job (ADR-166).

role.description: The role whose people look at a kept item and try it again or discard it.

description.description: Where a kept item is, what is kept with it, such as the error of its last try, and how a person finds it, in the design's words; the store a stack uses is the implementation's.

steps.description: What the person does with a kept item, in order, each with a check: look at it, then try it again or discard it.

gateway.description: SpecArch keyword. One gateway: the token it verifies before it reads anything else, the claim whose value selects the service, the table of forwards from a value to a dependency, the dependencies it calls besides, the middlewares it runs first and the refusals it answers in place of the forwarded service (ADR-141).

token.description: SpecArch keyword. The token the gateway verifies, by its key under tokens, with the meaning an operation's token has: its format, its signature algorithm and its claims are the token's own (ADR-097). When the claim is aud, the forwards are the token's fixed audience, so its aud declares no const or enum, it is not the default, and no operation names it (ADR-141).

claim.description: RFC 7519 keyword. The name of the claim, one the token declares under claims, whose value selects the service; it is read from the verified token only. A claim whose value is a list, as aud may be, selects a service when exactly one of its values is a forward's.

forwards.description: SpecArch keyword. The table of services, one row per value: value, the claim's value, and dependency, the key under dependencies of the service a request with that value is forwarded to, of kind system or identityProvider. Each value appears once. The dependency's timeout is how long the gateway waits for the service; where the service is in an environment is a server of the implementation file's deployment (ADR-136).

value.description: RFC 7519 keyword. The claim's value, for aud an absolute URI naming the service (RFC 8707, section 2).

dependency.description: SpecArch keyword. The dependency the request is forwarded to, by its key under dependencies.

calls.description: SpecArch keyword. The dependencies the gateway calls besides the ones it forwards to, as an operation's calls: the identity provider whose keys it fetches among them. A forward's dependency is not listed here too.

middlewares.description: SpecArch keyword. The middlewares the gateway runs before its own steps, in the order they run, by their names under middlewares; an empty list says it runs none.

refusals.description: SpecArch keyword. What the gateway answers itself, in place of the forwarded service's answer, in a middleware's form: a status, the problem type under errors and the condition.

problem.description: The problem type under errors that the refusal names.

menuItem.description: SpecArch keyword. One entry of a menu: a leaf that opens a page, or a group of entries.

page.description: The page the entry opens; it is shown to who may open the page.

valueObject.description: An object schema with no key: JSON Schema's properties and required, and nothing that only a stored record has (a primary key, relations, constraints, states).

properties.description: JSON Schema keyword. The schema's fields.

view.description: SpecArch keyword. A read model: the entity it reads from, whose every field it carries, and the properties it adds. It may be the item of a response and, when it carries no rows, the subject of a list; never the body of a request.

from.description: The entity the view reads from; the view holds one row per record of it.

properties.description: The fields the view adds, keyed by camelCase name; none may repeat a field of the entity.

viewProperty.description: A field a view adds: exactly one of path, relations separated by dots that each lead to one record and end in a field of the last; count, a relation of the entity that leads to many records; or rows, a one-to-many relation of the entity whose records the view carries. A path has its field's type and is null when a relation has no record; a count is a 64-bit integer and leaves out softly deleted records; rows are a list of the relation's target, softly deleted records left out, and empty when it has none.

caller.description: SpecArch keyword. The one caller record of a specification.

properties.description: JSON Schema keyword. The caller's properties, keyed by camelCase name, each typed as a field; a property the caller may lack, such as a member identifier a staff member has none of, allows null, and a comparison with it is false when it is null.

tenant.description: SpecArch keyword. The one tenant scope of a specification.

property.description: SpecArch keyword. The caller's property that names the caller's tenant, such as organisationId.

key.description: SpecArch keyword. The field every tenant-owned entity carries, compared with the caller's property; an entity with a field of this name is a tenant's.

shared.description: SpecArch keyword. The entities every tenant reads whole, such as a list of countries; each carries no field named key.

clientName.description: kebab-case software_id of a client; people, nobody and public are reserved.

proof.description: SpecArch keyword. How a client proves its identity on each request: signedRequest, a signature over named parts of the request after RFC 9421 with the algorithm the two sides agree on and the components it covers; mutualTls, the client certificate of RFC 8705; token, a token format declared under tokens; spiffe, an X.509 or JWT SVID carrying the SPIFFE ID; or wimse, the Workload Identity Token of the WIMSE drafts. A service in a chain presents a workload identity: mutualTls, spiffe or wimse. The key itself is a secret and is never in a specification.

algorithm.description: For signedRequest: an algorithm RFC 9421 registers, such as hmac-sha256, ecdsa-p256-sha256 or ed25519; design, not stack, because the client cannot sign without knowing it.

covers.description: For signedRequest: the covered components, as RFC 9421 names them: @method, @path and the other derived components, or a header field by its name in lower case, such as content-digest or date.

token.description: For a token proof: the token format the client presents, a name under tokens; never a transaction token, since a workload must not authenticate itself with one (the draft, section 13.12).

client.description: SpecArch keyword. One client: its kind, the versions it is admitted at, the roles it holds and its proof.

kind.description: application, where a person signs in, or service, a program that calls on its own account or carries a person's call. Neither word is a role: what a client may do is its roles' permissions.

softwareVersion.description: SpecArch keyword. The versions the client is admitted at: a lower bound included and an upper bound excluded, each a Semantic Versioning 2.0.0 version, written ">=1.2.0 <2.0.0". Checked once, at the edge, against the softwareVersion claim of the token the issuer fills from the registration; a specification whose tokens declare no such claim is refused (software_version). A refusal is 403 with the problem the design declares, never 426 (ADR-106).

softwareStatement.description: SpecArch keyword. True when the version is the publisher's, asserted in the signed software statement of RFC 7591, section 2.3, that the issuer verified at registration, so that the version check is a security check; false or left out, the version is self-asserted (section 5) and the check is a compatibility check, which is what a browser or a phone can offer.

roles.description: The roles the client holds when it calls on its own account; a client with roles must have a proof. A service with neither only carries a person's call.

store.description: The dependency every module writes its security events to, append-only.

alarm.description: The dependency that is the alarm channel.

claim.description: JSON Schema keywords of one claim, as a field has them; a registered claim of the JSON Web Token Claims registry is written as the registry names it, carries the registry's type and is not retyped.

oneOf.description: A type that also allows null, written as JSON Schema does: [string, 'null'].

format.description: The concrete type of the value, where the JSON type alone would leave it open. type says how the value is carried in JSON; format says what it is. An integer needs int32, int64 or uint64; a number needs double; a decimal is a string with format decimal, precision and scale; an int64 or uint64 that can exceed 2^53 is carried as a string with format int64 or uint64. See 'Types' in docs/conventions.md.

properties.description: For an object claim such as tctx: its members, each a claim.

expression.description: A bool expression over the token's claims, in the subset of docs/conventions.md, checked wherever the token is accepted.

format.description: jwt (RFC 7519) or opaque, a reference the service looks up.

tokenType.description: SpecArch keyword. access_token, the default, or txn_token, the suffix of the OAuth token type identifier of a transaction token, which is a JWT carried in the Txn-Token header and never in Authorization, declares the draft's claims txn, sub, scope and req_wl, and has no aud, since its audience is the trust domain (ADR-111).

signature.description: For a JWT: an algorithm of RFC 7518 or RFC 8037, such as ES256, RS256, EdDSA or HS256; none is refused, as RFC 8725 says a verifier must refuse it. Design, because the verifier is often another service.

claims.description: JSON Schema properties, camelCase like every property and on the wire as info.wireNames says, except the registered claims (iss, sub, aud, exp, nbf, iat, jti; act, scope, client_id, may_act; cnf; txn, events, toe; auth_time, acr, amr, azp; and the Transaction Tokens draft's req_wl, rctx and tctx), written as the registry names them and carrying its types. aud with const or enum fixes the audience an access token is accepted for. A claim fills the caller's property of the same name.

checks.description: SpecArch keyword. Rules over the claims, each a derived red case wherever the token is accepted.

default.description: SpecArch keyword. True on the one token every operation accepts unless it names another with token.

permissionReference.description: SpecArch keyword. A permission of another module, the one whose service enforces it: <dependency>#/permissions/<name>, through a dependency that names that module's specification (ADR-107).

clientReference.description: SpecArch keyword. A client of the identity module: <dependency>#/clients/<software_id>, through a dependency that names the identity module's specification (ADR-107).
